newsitem.title: IRAN: Iran releases director of critical Islamic weekly.
newsitem.headline: Iran releases director of critical Islamic weekly.

text.p: Iranian authorities have freed on bail the director of a critical hardline Islamic magazine who was arrested after the magazine challenged a publication ban, a staff member of the weekly said on Tuesday.

The staff member told Reuters that Heshmatollah Tabarzadi, director of Payam-e Daneshjoo (Student's Message), was released on bail on Saturday, a week after his arrest. The staff member did not say how much the bail was.
A court in July banned Tabarzadi from running the magazine for five years and ordered him to pay 10 million rials ($3,300) in fines for "publishing lies and causing public confusion".
But the magazine's staff recently distributed photocopies of the weekly on a limited scale, arguing that the court ruling did not include a publication ban.
"He was arrested on a complaint by the (Culture and Islamic) Guidance Ministry's Press Review Board which believes that there is a publication ban against us," the staff member said.
"The board has promised to rule on our case within two weeks. Now, we will just wait and see before publishing again," the staff member, who declined to be named, said.

Payam-e Daneshjoo, run by hardline students, had gained popularity by criticising President Akbar Hashemi Rafsanjani's aides and reform policies and publishing stories about economic hardships of the people and alleged corruption in high places.
($1=3,000 rials at the official exchange rate)
